assertions.description: A second import() of a module URL whose fetch failed (HTTP 404) issues a real second network request instead of rejecting from the module map cache.
assertions.test: (async () => { const u = new URL('/v156/avoid-caching-module-failures/modules/conf-missing-' + Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8) + '.js', location.origin).href; const count = () => performance.getEntriesByType('resource').filter((e) => e.name === u).length; const settle = (before) => new Promise((res) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const tick = () => { if (count() > before || performance.now() - t0 > 1500) res(); else setTimeout(tick, 60); }; setTimeout(tick, 60); }); for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { const before = count(); try { await import(u); } catch (e) { /* expected */ } await settle(before); } return count() >= 2; })()

assertions.description: Both import() attempts of a still-broken URL reject with a TypeError; the change makes the retry reach the network, not succeed by magic.
assertions.test: (async () => { const u = new URL('/v156/avoid-caching-module-failures/modules/conf-missing2-' + Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8) + '.js', location.origin).href; let rejections = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { try { await import(u); } catch (e) { if (e instanceof TypeError) rejections++; } await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 250)); } return rejections === 2; })()

assertions.description: A module served with HTTP 200 that fails to parse is NOT refetched by a second import(): only network and status failures became retryable, parse failures still produce a cached errored module script.
assertions.test: (async () => { const u = new URL('/v156/avoid-caching-module-failures/modules/parse-error.js?conf=' + Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8), location.origin).href; const count = () => performance.getEntriesByType('resource').filter((e) => e.name === u).length; const settle = (before) => new Promise((res) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const tick = () => { if (count() > before || performance.now() - t0 > 1500) res(); else setTimeout(tick, 60); }; setTimeout(tick, 60); }); let rejections = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { const before = count(); try { await import(u); } catch (e) { rejections++; } await settle(before); } return rejections === 2 && count() === 1; })()

assertions.description: A healthy module imported twice resolves both times from a single network fetch: successful module map entries remain cached as before.
assertions.test: (async () => { const u = new URL('/v156/avoid-caching-module-failures/modules/stable.js?conf=' + Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8), location.origin).href; const count = () => performance.getEntriesByType('resource').filter((e) => e.name === u).length; let ok = 0; for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) { try { const m = await import(u); if (m.answer === 42) ok++; } catch (e) { /* fail below */ } await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 250)); } return ok === 2 && count() === 1; })()

assertions.description: A module that failed on a flaky network is recoverable by a later import() once the network heals, without reloading the page.
assertions.test: Requires a network layer that fails then recovers; run the service-worker-driven scenario interactively on the flaky-network-recovery concept page and confirm the retry mounts the widget.
